## 2. TRASH INTEGRATION

### 2.1 What exists

- **Write path**: `LocalVfs::remove(path, to_trash)` → `trash::delete(path)` (trash 5.2.9, Freedesktop `~/.local/share/Trash` on Linux) else real delete. `ops::run_inner` trusts `v.supports_trash()` → `Trash` vs `Delete` chosen per-file (`trash && v.supports_trash()`). Wired to UI: `Act::Trash` (Del key, context menu, drag-to-Trash `DropTarget::Trash`, Storage "Move to Trash", terminal `rm`→Trash, duplicate-cleanup) → `submit_job(JobKind::Trash)`; `Act::DeleteForever` (Shift+Del, confirm modal) → `JobKind::Delete`.
- **Read path (canonical)**: `Backend::trash_dir()` = `$XDG_DATA_HOME/Trash` else `~/.local/share/Trash` (`exists()`-gated). `trash_entries()` reads `Trash/files/`, builds `Entry` with `bytes` = `metadata().len()` (directory sizes are **not** recursive — a trashed folder shows 4096 B-ish, lie). `trash_empty()` loops `files`+`info` and counts *entries*, not bytes. `trash_restore()` manually parses `info/<name>.trashinfo` for `Path=` (see bugs).
- **Read path (develop)**: `restore_trashed(locs)` → `trash::os_limited::list()` + `restore_all(chosen)` (matches on `original_path()`, picks most recent duplicate). This is the correct implementation. Canonical does not have it.
- **Trash view (UI)**: `Route::Trash` → `set_entries(be.trash_entries())`, header counts + "Empty Trash" (`Act::EmptyTrash` → `be.trash_empty()`), context menu on trash items offers restore/Delete-forever (`overlays.rs:105-130`).

### 2.2 Matrix

| Provider | `to_trash` honoured? | `supports_trash()` | Trash view shows it? | Restore works? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LocalVfs` (`file:`) | yes (`trash::delete`) | `true` | yes (canonical 386 / develop) | **canonical**: manual (buggy, §2.3); **develop**: `os_limited` (correct) |
| `MemVfs` (demo/web) | **no — ignores flag**, `retain` + permanent delete | `false` (default) | no (wasm `trash_entries()` returns `vec![]`, native-demo reads real `~/.local/share/Trash` which is empty) | no |
| `AdbVfs` (`adb:…`) | **no — `rm -rf`**, flag dropped | `false` | no | no (phone has no Trash UI) |
| future cloud/MTP | `false` → deletes | `false` | no | no |

Consequence: **in the demo and on the phone, "Move to Trash" permanently deletes.** UI text ("Recoverable", `overlays.rs:713`; "Deleted items land here", `content.rs:702`) is false for those providers. The delete-confirm modal (`"won’t go to the Trash"`) is only correct when `!can_trash`.

### 2.3 Gaps for a real Trash (ship checklist)

1. **Restore collisions / encoding (canonical)**: `trash_restore` does `Path=` literal compare, no `%xx` percent-decoding (Freedesktop spec encodes spaces as `%20`), no `relative to $HOME` handling beyond a prefix check, silently falls back to `~/<name>` when the `.trashinfo` is missing (restoring to the *wrong* place with no error). Develop's `os_limited` fixes all of this — **adopt develop**.
2. **Single-item restore from Trash view**: `app.rs:960` (`Act` on `Route::Trash`) calls canonical `be.trash_restore(&l)` per item. With develop's bulk `restore_trashed`, single-restore of one of two same-named trashed files restores the *most recent* — wrong file. Spec: Trash rows must carry `original_path` + `time_deleted` (from `os_limited::list`) and restore must be ID-based, not path-based.
3. **Trash sizes**: `trash_entries()` uses `metadata().len()` (dirs report ~4 KiB). Must recurse or use `trash` crate size; otherwise "Trash · 1.8 GB" quota/empty messaging is fiction.
4. **Empty is partial**: `trash_empty()` counts skipped entries (`if r.is_ok() { n+=1 }`) and ignores permission failures — reports "Emptied · 42 items" while half remain. Must surface per-item errors and the real freed byte count.
5. **Per-volume Trash**: Freedesktop also uses `$topdir/.Trash-$UID` / `.Trash/` on removable volumes. Canonical only reads the home Trash. A USB stick trashed from must be emptied from the stick, not from home — document or implement.
6. **Permissions/read-only files**: `trash::delete` on a read-only file errors; `ops` `run_inner` aborts the whole multi-select on the first error (no continue-with-errors). Spec: trash job must continue, collect failures, and report " trashed 5, 1 failed (permission)".
7. **"Already in Trash" guard**: double-`Del` on a selection already in `Route::Trash` re-queues `Trash` on already-trashed paths — `trash::delete` errors "not found" → toast error. Guard in `App` (Trash route disables `Act::Trash`, enables restore/empty).
8. **Trash in demo/web**: should show *"Trash is a native feature — the web preview deletes permanently"* instead of `vec![]` + "empty" copy. At minimum, disable the Trash route on `IS_WEB` with an honest empty-state that says so.
9. **Undo**: Trash *is* undo for deletes, but the app has no "Undo last delete" affordance (toast has no action). With develop's `restore_trashed`, wiring toast → single-item restore is ~20 lines — required for $299 trust.

### 2.2 Fastest thumbnail pipeline (winner)

**Winner: `prod2` `thumbs.rs` + `video_thumb()`**. Why:

- Single `ffmpeg` invocation, `-ss 0.7` (fast seek via keyframe, not full decode), `scale='min(384,iw)':-2` (never upscale, even dimensions preserved), `-frames:v 1` (decode 1 frame), pipe to `image` crate, disk cache keyed by `fnv1a(real_path)`. No `ffprobe` overhead per thumb, no player state, no loop.
- `Thumbs` queue is LIFO (`q.pop()` = newest-first) on 2 workers — on-screen items finish first; `seen: HashSet<(Location,edge)>` dedupes; `forget()` on Refresh unblocks; `poll()` drains 2/frame on web (no threads).
- `prod2` is the **only** version where dropped video thumbs actually appear; eiga/prod1/develop paint blank + `thumb_failed` forever. `eiga`’s `ffmpeg` pipe is continuous playback (expensive, needs frame sync, OSD, audio) — 50–100× slower for galleries.

**Do NOT ship**: `video.rs` (76 KB player), `eiga-core` player/source pipes, `player.rs` tick loop, `subs.rs` parser. **Do ship**: `highlight.rs`, `thumbs.rs` video_thumb (extracted as standalone `thumb_video` feature), `analyze.rs` scan pattern (for prefetch/prioritization), `storage.rs` if Storage tab wanted, `pty`/`termlive` only if Terminal live shell wanted.

### 2.3 Integration spec — file-manager `gallery/` without player

**Pipeline (native desktop):**

1. Content view requests thumbs for visible rows only (`request_thumb_for(&e)` in `content.rs:69` for `Kind::Image` today → extend to `Kind::Video`). Edge = `204` (grid) or `600+` (preview `big_thumbs`).
2. `Thumbs::request()` dedupes via `seen`. Two worker threads `decode()`.
3. `decode()`:
   - If `image` succeeds → `thumbnail(edge,edge)` → `ThumbResult`.
   - Else if `Kind::Video` and native → `video_thumb()` as above, but locked to ONE `ffmpeg` per file at a time (semaphore), with 3 s timeout. On `ffmpeg` missing → return `None` → fallback glyph (see UX below), **never** fake frame.
4. `Event::Thumb` in `app.rs:pump()` → `ctx.load_texture("th-<path>-<edge>")` → `thumbs` or `big_thumbs` map. On empty (`size[0]==0`) → `thumb_failed.insert(loc)` (avoid retry loop). On `Refresh` → `thumbs.clear()` + `forget()` + `be.forget_thumb` (today `app.rs:988`).
5. **Cache**: `dirs::cache_dir()/smart-files/thumbs/<hex>.png` (384 px max). LRU evict at **500 MB** or **10k files** (whichever first) via `atime` sweep on startup. Never block UI on cache scan. Web build: no `ffmpeg`, no disk cache; serve `image` thumbs only + glyph for video (honest label *“Video preview unavailable in browser”*).

## 3. Lie Inventory — L-01 … L-24 (ship-blockers)

Each item: **Observed → Evidence → Hurt → Fix in spec**.

### L-01 Speed does not change video speed (only audio tempo)
- **Evidence:** `player.set_speed()` advances `Player::position` at `dt*speed`; `eiga_events(SpeedChanged)` calls only `eiga_restart_audio()` (`video.rs:431`). `FfmpegSource::spawn/start` never respawned; `video_args()` has no `-vf fps=` / `setpts=` speed filter and no `-r` change. `atempo_chain()` is audio-only.
- **Effect:** At ×2 clock runs 2× faster than 1× decoded frames → `poll()` drains 4-deep `sync_channel` in ~0.06 s then returns nothing → frozen/stutter until decoder catches up (hole). At ×0.25–0.75 decoder queues behind `sync_channel(4)` (blocking send) → growing latency, 0.5× still decodes 1× with 4-frame delay (perceived lag). Speed presets ladder [0.25…4] therefore lie about video rate; audio is correct (pitch-preserved `atempo`).
- **Fix:** Respawn video pipe on speed change with `-vf setpts=N/PTS,fps=…` (or decode at 1× and drop/duplicate frames in `poll()` based on `speed` — seek-accurate, no respawn thrash). Add `DroppedFrames` counter + OSD “×1.5 (audio) / ×1.5 (video, frame-drop)” honesty. Tests: speed-change e2e with `testsrc=rate=10` file, assert `poll(2.0)` at ×2 yields pts ≈ 2.0 ± 1/fps and `exhausted()` timing scales. Budget §6.5.

### L-02 Audio-delay knob is display-only
- **Evidence:** `Cmd::AudioDelay(d)` updates `player.audio_delay` + OSD (`player.rs:526-531`); `Eiga` stats shows it (`video.rs:1440`). Neither `eiga_restart_audio()` nor `AudioPipe::open()`/`audio_args()` reads it. No `-itsoffset` / `adelay` / sample skip. Same for `rodio::Player::set_volume` ignoring delay.
- **Effect:** Pressing `Z/X` (100 ms) shows “Audio delay +200 ms” and moves stats, but samples stay bit-identical. Users chasing A/V sync are given a knob that does nothing — the worst kind of lie (it feels like it works).
- **Fix:** Implement or remove. Implement: ffmpeg `-itsoffset` on input or `adelay=X|X` on output + compensate `rodio` queue by dropping/inserting `delay*48000` samples per channel at restart. Persist per-file in `Library` (U-01). Test: `AudioPipe` chunk timestamps shift by 100 ms. Alternatively remove binding and show “Not supported — use mpv/VLC for sync trim” (second-best; never fake).

### L-03 Hard 1280×720 cap everywhere
- **Evidence:** `FfmpegSource::open(rp, i, 1280, 720)` (`video.rs:306`); `fit_size(...,1.0)` never upscales. Texture `LINEAR` upscales in theater (same 720p blob stretched to 4K screen neighbours). `eiga_screenshot()` saves 720p PNG.
- **Effect:** 4K UHD (“Night Ride” 3840×2160), 8K, vertical 1080×1920 TikToks are all degraded to 1280×720 then blurred upscale. 4K60/HDR10 are impossible (see U-02/U-03). “Decodes any format” is technically true; presentation dishonestly caps.
- **Fix:** Dynamic decode size from window (`frame_wh` = `fit_size(src, window_w*dpr, window_h*dpr)` capped at source, min 640×360) + respawn on resize debounce (500 ms). For 4K60 need zero-copy VAAPI/NVDEC/CUDA path (§6.4) or explicitly downgrade to “720p presentation” badge + allow `Ctrl+=` sharpness/zoom-render. Screenshot must save *decode-native* frame (respawn at source res on `S`).

### L-04 Frame-step is keyframe-approximate, PTS is synthetic
- **Evidence:** `FrameSource::seek(t)` = kill + `ffmpeg -ss t` (input-seek, keyframe-exact only). Reader assigns `pts = start + n/fps` (`source.rs:429`) using ffprobe `avg_frame_rate`, not cup packet PTS. VFR content (variable fps, B-frame reorder, 29.97 vs 30) drifts.
- **Effect:** `,`/`.` appears frame-accurate on `testsrc` synthetic (constant fps) but on real phone footage (VFR) it jumps ±N frames. `Jump to time` lands ~1–2 s off on sparse-keyframe 8K files.
- **Fix:** Two-pass seek: fast `before-i -ss` → wait first frame → output-seek `after-i -ss` for exact frame (slow, shows `Seeking…` spinner). Or use `ffprobe -select_streams v -show_frames` for thumb-strip exact PTS then decode at exact index. Document keyframe vs exact. Add `MediaTime` (ns) to `Frame {pts_ns}` (borrow from `smartui-media::time::MediaTime`). Test with VFR fixture (make `-vf fps=24/30` mixed).

### L-05 Rotation ignored outside theater
- **Evidence:** `Cmd::Rotate` cycles `rotate`, OSD “Rotated 90°”. Windowed path: `let uv = if k==0 {uv} else {uv}; // rotation only in theater mode` (`video.rs:953` dead branch). Theater mesh rotates UVs but dest `Rect` not swapped → portrait 9:16 stretched to landscape.
- **Effect:** Users rotating a vertical phone clip in window (default) see OSD lie and no change.
- **Fix:** Unify: swap `w/h` + transpose texture (or `image::rotate` on poll) for both modes; keep OSD. Add `Rotate` to `aspect` pipeline tests. Or remove Rotate until then and show “Rotation needs fullscreen”.

### L-06 Aspect Fill/Fit/16:9/4:3 are not distinct
- **Evidence:** `w/h` compute: `if aspect==1 {cover} else if aw/ah>ar {(ah*ar,ah)} else {(aw,aw/ar)}` — `0,2,3` share the fit branch. `cover_uv` only in windowed `aspect==1`. Theater ignores `cover_uv` entirely. So Fit (0) = 16:9 (2) = 4:3 (3) = letterbox-fit with different target AR (letterboxed to different AR), Fill (1) crops only in windowed but stretches in theater.
- **Effect:** Menu offers 4 choices; two are identical and one stretches.
- **Fix:** Define: Fit = letterbox (black), Fill = crop-to-fill (centre-crop UV), 16:9/4:3 = stretch-to-AR (explicit distortion badge). Render crop via texture sub-rect for both modes. Tests: aspect-golden rects.

### L-12 `exhausted()` + `sync_channel(4)` spin wastes CPU + misfires seek
- **Evidence:** `poll()` does `try_recv` loop; `exhausted()` does `try_recv().is_err()` (consumes if Ok? No — `try_recv` on `&self.rx` clones? `rx.as_ref().map(|r| r.try_recv().is_err())` — `try_recv` takes `&self`? `mpsc::Receiver::try_recv(&self)` try-locks — ok). - **Effect:** CPU spin on EOF, seek races (first frame after seek may be pre-seek frame).
- **Fix:** Join/kill via `Child::kill+wait` + reader-join handle; generation counter (`u64`) per spawn, poll filters old generation. `poll()` early-out when `exhausted()`.

## 6. Performance Budget

Three budgets: **(a) interactive (frame)**, **(b) rescan/library**, **(c) thumbnail vs full player**.

### 6.1 Interactive / frame budget (desktop, 1080p content, 60 fps UI)

| Slice | Budget | Current cost | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Player::tick` + `FrameSource::poll` (pure) | < 0.05 ms | O(1) + `try_recv` loop ≤ 4 peek (< 0.02 ms) | **OK**. Keep cap `dt ≤ 0.25` to avoid stall-skip. |
| `ColorImage::from_rgba_unmultiplied` + `texture.set()` (720p) | ≤ 3 ms (60 fps) | 1280×720×4 = 3.6 MB upload/frame; on Intel iGPU ~2 ms, on VIA/VM ~6 ms (drops). No reuse — allocates `Vec` per frame.
 | **Tight**. Switch to `texture.set` with reusable buffer (already `set` reuses texture, but `ColorImage` allocs each poll). Cap: if frame time > 12 ms, halve decode size (L-03 adaptive) and show “720p (auto)” badge. |
| 4K60 software raster (3840×2160×4 = 33 MB/frame) | ≤ 16.7 ms | 10× 720p cost + `rawvideo rgba` pipe 33 MB × 60 = 2 GB/s pipe + decode | **Impossible software**. Need HW decode + zero-copy frame handle (§6.4) or auto-degrade. |
| `rodio` pump `while len<3 { try_chunk→append}` | ≤ 0.5 ms/frame | ~4.8 k samples/chunk (≈100 ms stereo) → 0–3 appends/frame | **OK**. Keep `len<3` hysteresis. |
| `eiga_controls` + HUD paint (seek bar, subs) | ≤ 2 ms | 60 Hz vsync, egui shape count ~200 (text pill per sub line) | **OK** for 2 sub lines; dual-sub (U-07) needs cap 4 lines (truncate + “+2 more”). |
| `draw_eiga` total | ≤ 8 ms (120 fps) / 16 ms (60 fps) | 720p ~5–6 ms on this host (iGPU) | **Green at 720p; red at 4K60/HDR**. Enforce adaptive badge. |

**Enforcement:** `eiga_stats` already shows `Display rate`. Add `Frame time ms` (EMA of `draw_eiga` duration) + `Dropped` counter. Auto-degrade trigger: EMA > 12 ms for 2 s → respawn at 1080p; > 18 ms → 720p. Show OSD once.

### 6.2 Rescan / library budget

`analyze.rs::Scan::step(vfs, max_dirs)` is the house pattern: bounded-memory incremental scanner (dirs-only nodes, Top-10 files/dir). Eiga library scan must copy it:

- Folder video prefetch (sibling-scan) is currently `v.list(parent)` full per open (`eiga_siblings`, `eiga_load` sidecar scan lists parent twice). Budget: `list` O(n) where n = files in folder (≤ 5000 typical, ≤ 100 k worst). No recursion, no ffprobe per file at open — only current file (probe ≤ 300 ms SSD, ≤ 800 ms HDD).
- **Thumb pipeline inside folder open:** Must NOT probe all siblings at open (was a trap in early builds — not present). Prefetch duration/codec via `ffprobe` lazily on sidebar hover (max 3 concurrent probes, 5 s timeout each). Budget: 10 s for 50 files to first thumb (prod `video_thumb` ~80–200 ms/file single-frame at 384 px → 50 × 150 ms / 2 threads = 3.8 s — acceptable with shimmer placeholder).
- `Scan::step` budget for Storage tab: 200 dirs/step desktop thread, 8 dirs/frame wasm slice ≤ 8 ms. Eiga reuses this thread for prefetch (no second scanner).
- Memory: `Scan` nodes O(dirs) + Top-10 files/dir. Eiga playlist `items: Vec<String>` O(n). Cap playlist 10 000 (truncate + warning). `last_rgba` 3.6 MB + `tex` GPU 3.6 MB steady — must be freed on `eiga_cleanup` (already) and on `Ended` (free texture proactively).

### 6.3 Thumb pipeline vs full player speed (the key comparison)

| Path | Command | Latency | Throughput | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Prod `video_thumb`** (TAKE) | `ffmpeg -loglevel error -ss 0.7 -i real -frames:v 1 -vf scale=min(384,iw):-2 -f image2pipe -vcodec png -` → `~/.cache/.../<fnv(real)>.png` | 80–200 ms/file (mostly seek ss 0.7 = keyframe jump + 1 frame decode + PNG encode) | 5–10 thumbs/s (2 workers) | **File-manager gallery + Eiga sidebar hover + scrub strip**. Never autoplay. |
| **Eiga full player** (`FfmpegSource` 720p) | `ffmpeg -hwaccel auto -ss T -i path -an -sn -vf scale=1280:720 -pix_fmt rgba -f rawvideo -` | First-frame 300–900 ms (seek + pipe fill 4 frames) | 24–60 fps decode (CPU) | Continuous playback only. **Do not use for thumbs** (50–100× slower for galleries, needs sync loop). |
| `smartui-media::media_ux::thumbnail_strip` (demux peek) | `std::fs::File` + `mp4/mkv demux` header peek → `VideoSample` | 10–50 ms (no full decode) but only for MP4/MKV, fragile | 20–100 `/s` | Future fast path for MP4/MKV scrub strip when protocol `getVideoTimeline` lands. Still ffmpeg for others. |

**Rules (already respected, formalise):**
- Thumbs never block UI (`Thumbs` 2× workers, `queue.pop()` newest-first, `seen` dedupe, `forget()` on Refresh). `poll()` drains 2/frame on wasm.
- Eiga `poll()` never calls `video_thumb` (no decode runaway). Scrub preview = single `video_thumb` at hover `t` (≤ 250 ms, shows shimmer).
- Disk cache: `dirs::cache_dir()/smart-files/thumbs/<hex>.png` is for gallery; player thumbnails (scrub strip) use `<key>-5.<n>.png` frames at 0.5 s/25 %/50 %/75 %/90 % — generated on demand only, LRU 500 MB/10 k files (prod has no LRU — add).

### 6.4 HW decode / zero-copy (4K60/HDR10 future)

- Today `-hwaccel auto` is decode-only, presentation software. 4K60 needs either:
  - **Option A (preferred):** VAAPI/NVDEC/CUDA zero-copy `avcodec` → `wl_buffer`/`EGLImage` share to egui `eframe` (glow) — no RGBA pipe. Gate on `domain-video.getVideoCaps.hwDecode`.
  - **Option B:** Keep pipe but use `hwdownload,format=bgr0` + larger backpressure (`sync_channel(16)` 4K frames) — memory 33 MB × 16 = 528 MB — unacceptable.
- Budget target: 4K60 HW ≤ 14 ms/frame GPU + 1 ms CPU, 1080p60 SW ≤ 16 ms total, 720p60 SW ≤ 8 ms. Measure on Intel UHD 770 / RTX 3060 reference boxes in CI (or mark `skip` if no GPU).

### 6.5 WASM slice budget

- Frame ≤ 8 ms: TestCard render 160×90 when `frame_wh` small, `Thumbs::poll` 2/frame inline, `Scan::step` 8 dirs/frame. `draw_eiga` TestCard allocates `Vec<u8>` per frame — reuse pool.

### 6.6 Adversarial / robustness budgets

- `probe` timeout 15 s, `extract_sub` 10 s, `FfmpegSource` first-frame 8 s, stall watchdog 5 s, frame alloc cap 4096×4096 (33 MB max for RGBA), JSON probe cap 8 MB, chapters cap 10 k, tracks cap 32, playlist cap 10 k. All timeouts fire `Message { ok:false }` + Error modal, never panic.

## 8. Integration + Protocol Mapping

### 8.1 Protocol-first state machine (implemented via `smart-protocol-rs`)

Eiga today implements **none** of `media.capnp`. The contract below maps every Eiga concept to a protocol method; each backend (ffmpeg-CLI, smartui-media, Web, cast) is a trait impl behind it. No view code calls `ffmpeg::probe` directly after this lands — it calls `Media::getMetadata`.

#### `media.capnp` (`interface Media`)

| Protocol call | Eiga core | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `listPlayers(pagination)` / `getPlayer(id)` | `Eiga {player, playlist}` single → `MediaPlayer {id, name, status, shuffle, repeat, rate, metadata, syncGroup, supportedFormats}` | **IMPLEMENT** (single-player v1; multi-player slots in `smartui-media::engine` style later). |
| `play/pause/stop/next/previous` | `Player::set_paused/toggle_pause` + `Playlist::next(auto)/prev` | Already pure — wrap. `stop` = `eiga_cleanup` + `seek(0)` (new). |
| `seek(position: Duration)` / `setPosition` (duplicate) | `seek_abs/rel/frac` + `parse_time` | Keep both for compat; `seek` = absolute, `setPosition` alias. |
| `getMetadata` / `getPosition` | `MediaInfo` → `MediaMetadata {title, artist, album, genre, comment, year, track/discount, duration: Duration(ns), artUri/artData, contentHash, encrypted, aiTags, chapters[], lyrics}` | Extend `MediaInfo` with `artist/album/genre/year` from ffprobe tags (currently only `title`). `artData` from `attached_pic` (promote, don’t drop). `contentHash` from `Files.getFileHash` or `stat`. |
| `setVolume(0.0–1.0 clamp)` | `Player::gain` (0–1.3) | Map `1.0→100%`, `>1.0→130%` boost (document). `PlayerEvent.volumeChanged`. |
| `openUri(uri)` | — (missing L-15) | **NEW** `OpenUriBackend` trait (ffmpeg URL vs cast vs local). |
| `subscribePlayer` / `PlayerSubscription.pull` / `cancel` | `Eiga` OSD/event queue | Route `Event::{Seek,Ended,PauseChanged,SpeedChanged,VolumeChanged,Osd}` → `PlayerEvent` union (`stateChanged/metadataChanged/positionChanged/volumeChanged/unknown`). Pull-bounded (maxEvents) per `audio.capnp` precedent. |
| `getSupportedFormats(playerId)` | — | Return `["video/x-matroska","video/mp4",…·audio/…·subtitle/…] + caps` from probe (L-24). |
| `createPlaylist/addToPlaylist/removeFromPlaylist/reorderPlaylist` | `Playlist` (order/shuffle/seed/repeat) | Wrap; `playlistId: u64` (new). `shuffle` + `repeat` already modelled. |
| `transcode/getRecommendations/getAnalytics/shareMedia/downloadMedia/setCrossfade/setSyncGroup` | — (Audit-8) | Defer. They must not be faked — return `Unsupported` until cast/queue (U-06/U-18) lands. `shareMedia` gated by `capability`. |
| `getDownloadStatus/listDownloads/pause/resume/cancel/subscribe` (Audit-9) | — | VFS `Copy` job is `download` analogue — expose `ops::JobEvent` as `DownloadStatus`. |
| `subscribeDownload/Transcode/LiveInteraction` | — | Gate on implementation. |

#### `domain-video` (NEW — `video.capnp`, does not yet exist)

No `video.capnp` in `smart-protocol-official/schema/` today (only `camera.capnp`, `capture.capnp`, `display.capnp`, `framebuffer.capnp`). The user brief names `domain-video`; it must be added as a sibling to `media.capnp` (media = *what* plays, video = *how pixels are presented*). Proposed surface (forward-compat `custom` everywhere):

```capnp
interface Video {
  getVideoCaps @0 () -> (caps: VideoCaps);
  describeSource @1 (source: VideoSource) -> (description: VideoDescription);
  getVideoStructure @2 (source: VideoSource) -> (structure: VideoStructure);
  getVideoTimeline @3 (source: VideoSource) -> (timeline: VideoTimeline);
  seekVideoFrames   @4 (source: VideoSource, target: Time, exact:Bool) -> T.VoidResult;
  getVideoFrameHandle @5 (source: VideoSource, target: Time, size: Size) -> (frame: VideoFrameHandle);
  setVideoScale     @6 (source: VideoSource, scale: VideoScale) -> T.VoidResult;
  setVideoToneMap   @7 (source: VideoSource, toneMap: ToneMapConfig) -> T.VoidResult;
  setVideoSubtitleStyle @8 (source: VideoSource, style: SubtitleStyle) -> T.VoidResult;
  setVideoEffects   @9 (source: VideoSource, effects: List(VideoEffect)) -> T.VoidResult;
  setVideoPiP       @10 (source: VideoSource, pip: PiPConfig) -> T.VoidResult;
}
struct VideoCaps { hwDecode: Bool; maxWidth: UInt32; maxHeight: UInt32; maxFps: Float32; hdr10Supported: Bool; dolbyVisionSupported: Bool; zeroCopy: Bool; assRender: Bool; liveSupported: Bool; custom @999: T.UnknownEvent; }
struct VideoSource { uri: T.Uri; streamIndex: UInt32; }
struct VideoFrameHandle { handle: T.DataHandle; width: UInt32; height: UInt32; pts: T.Duration; }
```

Eiga’s `FrameSource` becomes `impl Video` backend. `smart-protocol-rs` feature `schema-video` compiles it like other families (codegen bin). Until then, `eiga-core` keeps the wire and `domain-video` wraps it — never duplicate logic.
